title: Palak Paneer
subtitle: Spiced spinach curry with fried cheese
excerpt: Feta is used here in place of paneer -- it holds its shape when fried and gives a creamy, milky contrast to the spiced spinach. It is saltier than paneer, so hold back on adding salt until you taste the finished dish. Pan-frying the feta first gives it a golden crust that keeps it intact in the sauce.
sourceNotes: Palak paneer is a North Indian dish in which fresh Indian cheese is simmered in a smooth, spiced spinach sauce. Paneer is traditionally made by curdling hot whole milk with lemon juice or vinegar; feta provides a similar texture in home cooking without the cheesemaking step.

content.text: Blend the spinach sauce until very smooth -- a coarse green puree is not the same dish. If you are using a hand blender, let the spinach cool slightly first. Feta is used here as a substitute for paneer and is saltier, so taste before adding any extra salt.

items.prepNote: fresh, or 400g frozen, fully defrosted and squeezed dry
cut into 2 cm cubes, used as a substitute for paneer

content.text: Blanch the fresh spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, drain, and refresh under cold water. Squeeze out as much water as possible. Blend to a smooth puree and set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp of ghee in the saucepan over medium-high heat. Fry the feta cubes in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden on two sides. Remove and set aside.

Add the remaining ghee to the pan. Cook the onion over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes. Add the cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds, then add the ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric, and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until the sauce has thickened. Add the spinach puree and stir well. Simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the double cream and garam masala.
Return the fried feta to the pan and fold gently. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to heat through. Taste for seasoning -- the feta is already salty, so add salt only if needed. Serve with rice or flatbread.

items.cause: Stirred too vigorously after adding to the spinach.
items.fix: Fold very gently and do not stir more than necessary. Paneer holds up better to heat than feta, so handle with care.
Blanch for 1 minute only and refresh immediately in cold water to preserve the colour and flavour.
